story.security.defaultNotice: jsoneo.parse() executes generated JavaScript code. Only parse data produced by jsoneo.stringify() from trusted sources. Never parse untrusted user input or arbitrary strings. This playground uses a curated fixture whitelist.
story.security.detailedNotice: jsoneo.parse() executes generated JavaScript code. Only parse data produced by jsoneo.stringify() from trusted sources. Never parse untrusted user input, network data from untrusted sources, or arbitrary strings. jsoneo is NOT a sandbox or security boundary. For untrusted data exchange, use native JSON or other data-only formats.
story.security.intendedUsage: This is the intended usage pattern
story.security.incorrectUsage: ❌ Incorrect Usage: Never Parse Untrusted Data
story.security.rule1: Only parse data produced by jsoneo.stringify()
story.security.rule2: Only parse data from trusted sources (your own application, controlled test fixtures)
story.security.rule3: Never parse user input, API responses from untrusted services, or arbitrary strings
story.security.rule4: jsoneo is NOT a sandbox — it uses new Function() to evaluate generated code
story.security.rule5: For untrusted data exchange, use native JSON.parse() or other data-only formats
story.security.rule6: If you must parse external data, validate/sanitize it first and understand the risks
story.roundTrip.bothFunctions: Both functions (bodies may differ, closure not captured)
story.meta.primitiveValues: JSON-compatible primitives: string, number, boolean, null, array, plain object.
story.meta.specialValues: JavaScript-specific special values that native JSON cannot represent: undefined, NaN, Infinity, -Infinity, -0, BigInt.
story.meta.builtinsCollections: Built-in objects and collections: Date, RegExp, URL, URLSearchParams, Map, Set.
story.meta.binaryValues: Binary data types: TypedArrays, ArrayBuffer, DataView. Node.js Buffer support (converted to Uint8Array in browsers).
story.meta.functionsClosure: Function serialization and deserialization. Function bodies are preserved but lexical closures are NOT captured automatically. Use the closure option to provide external variables.
story.meta.descriptorsPrototype: Custom property descriptors (writable, enumerable, configurable, getters/setters) and prototype chain handling.
story.meta.circularReferences: Circular reference handling. jsoneo tracks circular references during serialization and restores them during parsing.
story.meta.options: StringifyOptions and ParseOptions demonstration. Shows how options affect serialization and deserialization behavior. Switch between presets or tune every option interactively.
story.meta.compatibility: Browser and Node.js compatibility. Shows which features are available in each environment and how jsoneo handles differences.
story.meta.securityBoundary: Security boundary demonstration. jsoneo.parse() executes generated JavaScript code. This page shows the correct and incorrect ways to use jsoneo, and why you must only parse trusted data.
